objective_for_doctor: A 4-year-old Female patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have a fever, been coughing up blood, and a cough.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’ve had a fever and a cough, and I’ve been coughing up blood. My throat really hurts, especially on the right side—my tonsil and the area in my throat near the thyroid cartilage feel painful too, and my nose is kind of congested or runny.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—when did the cough and the blood start, and is the blood just streaks in phlegm or are you spitting larger amounts?  
Doctor: Do you have trouble breathing, wheezing, or fast breathing, and have you had any recent choking episode or swallowed something (like a small toy/piece of food)?

The cough and these symptoms started today, I think. The blood is in my phlegm—more like streaks, not big amounts. I don’t have trouble breathing or wheezing, and no choking or swallowed anything that I know of.

Doctor: I’ll examine your throat and neck for swelling or pus—do you have a high fever (≥38.5°C), do you have a muffled “hot potato” voice or difficulty swallowing saliva?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Rapid_Strep_Test and REQUEST TEST: CBC; also, I’d like a REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray to look for pneumonia or other lung causes.
I don’t know the exact temperature, but I do have a fever. I don’t think my voice is “hot potato,” and I’m not having trouble swallowing my saliva.

Doctor: I’m going to look at your tonsils for exudate and check your neck lymph nodes/soft-tissue swelling—right now, do you have a rash, itchy eyes, or red lips/tongue, and have you had any ear pain?  
Doctor: Also, when you cough, does it feel painful deep in the chest or more on the throat, and are you able to drink and pee normally today?
I don’t have a rash, and my eyes aren’t itchy. I don’t have red lips or tongue. When I cough it feels more in my throat than deep in my chest, and I can drink and pee normally today.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—do you have any severe one-sided throat pain with trouble opening your mouth, neck swelling/tenderness, or drooling, and are your tonsils enlarged with any white patches?  
Doctor: Also, what’s your oxygen level if we measure it, and have you had any known exposure to strep/flu or recent vomiting?
I don’t have trouble opening my mouth, and I’m not drooling. I don’t know about oxygen level right now. I haven’t been vomiting, and I don’t know of any specific exposure to strep or flu.

Doctor: I’m going to check your tonsils and throat closely and listen to your lungs; can you tell me if your cough is mostly dry or wet, and do you have any nasal discharge (green/yellow) or facial pain? Also, please let me know if you’ve had any measured fever at home or any chills.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Oxygen_Saturation (pulse oximetry); REQUEST TEST: Throat_Exam documenting tonsillar exudate/uvula deviation; and REQUEST TEST: Influenza_Antigen_or_PCR.
My cough feels wet, not dry. I don’t have green or yellow nasal discharge, and I don’t have facial pain. I don’t know the measured fever at home, but I have had fever and some chills.

Doctor: With wet cough, fever/chills, and streaks of blood in phlegm, I’m concerned about an infectious source like pneumonia or severe bronchitis with airway irritation, but I need your oxygen level and throat exam findings first—your wet cough in a 4-year-old can still be pneumonia even without wheeze or breathing trouble.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Oxygen_Saturation (pulse oximetry); REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray (already ordered but I need results); REQUEST TEST: Throat_Exam findings (tonsillar exudate, uvula position); REQUEST TEST: Rapid_Strep_Test result; REQUEST TEST: CBC.

I don’t have the oxygen level or the chest x-ray/throat exam results yet—I haven’t seen them. I can tell you my cough is wet, I’ve had fever and chills, and my throat hurts a lot on the right side with tonsil pain.

Doctor: I need the results urgently—right now, are you able to get your oxygen saturation and the chest X-ray report, and does the throat exam show tonsillar pus/exudate or swollen cervical lymph nodes?  
Doctor: Also, is the right-sided throat pain worsening quickly, and do you have any trouble swallowing, drooling, or a muffled voice (even slightly)?  
Doctor: If the X-ray shows pneumonia or the throat swab is positive, we’ll treat accordingly—REQUEST TEST: Oxygen_Saturation, REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray_results, REQUEST TEST: Throat_Exam (exudate/uvula deviation/neck swelling), REQUEST TEST: Rapid_Strep_Test result.

I don’t have my oxygen saturation number, and I haven’t gotten the chest X-ray report yet. I don’t know the throat exam findings you’re asking about (like pus/exudate or uvula/neck swelling), and my right-sided throat pain feels like it’s been bad since it started today—but I don’t have trouble swallowing, drooling, or a muffled voice.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—given wet cough with fever/chills and streaks of blood in phlegm plus significant unilateral throat (tonsil) pain, the top concerns are pneumonia and/or streptococcal tonsillitis; I need one key exam result—please check and tell me your oxygen saturation right now (or let us measure), and confirm whether you have visible tonsillar exudate/white patches on the right.  
Doctor: Also, have you had any recent varicella (chickenpox) or a known bleeding disorder or frequent bruising, and any sick contacts with confirmed strep or flu in the last week?  
Doctor: If oxygen is low or the chest X-ray shows pneumonia, we’ll treat pneumonia; if strep/tonsillar exudate is positive, we’ll treat strep—REQUEST TEST: Oxygen_Saturation and REQUEST TEST: Rapid_Strep_Test (if not resulted).

I can’t give you an oxygen saturation number right now—please measure it. I also don’t know if there are visible white patches/exudate on my tonsil because I can’t really see it clearly myself. I haven’t had chickenpox, and I don’t know of any bleeding disorder or frequent bruising, and I don’t know of any confirmed strep or flu contacts in the last week.

Doctor: I’m going to listen to your lungs and check your tonsils/neck directly now; REQUEST TEST: Oxygen_Saturation (pulse oximetry) and REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray (result) and REQUEST TEST: Rapid_Strep_Test (result) because you have fever + wet cough with blood-streaked sputum.  
Doctor: While we wait, are you able to drink fluids normally and do you have any fast breathing or repeated coughing fits that make you vomit?  
Doctor: If your oxygen is low or the chest X-ray shows pneumonia, I’ll treat pneumonia; if your Rapid Strep is positive with tonsillar exudate, I’ll treat streptococcal tonsillitis.
Yes, I’m able to drink fluids normally. I don’t have fast breathing that I’ve noticed, and I haven’t vomited from coughing.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—your next step depends on your oxygen and the chest X-ray: can you report your oxygen saturation (%) from pulse oximetry, and what did the chest X-ray show (any “pneumonia/infiltrate” or “normal”)?  
Doctor: Also, do you have the Rapid Strep test result yet (positive/negative), and did the throat exam show tonsillar exudate/white patches?
I don’t have the oxygen saturation % or the chest X-ray results yet. I also don’t have the Rapid Strep result or the throat exam findings (like exudate/white patches) to tell you.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—while we urgently obtain your oxygen saturation, chest X-ray result, and Rapid Strep/throat exam findings, I need to know one more thing: when you cough up blood, is it only streaks in the mucus or have there been any larger clots/greater amounts?  
Doctor: Also, have you had any nosebleeds recently or gum bleeding (so we can tell if the blood is coming from the nose/mouth rather than the lungs)?
It’s only streaks in the mucus—no big clots or larger amounts. I haven’t had nosebleeds or gum bleeding recently.

Doctor: Thanks—streaks only and no nose/gum bleeding makes true hemoptysis more likely from the lower airways. I’ve already ordered key tests, but since I still don’t have your oxygen saturation and chest X-ray results, I must decide based on the pattern: fever + wet cough + chills + blood-streaked sputum with no breathing distress suggests **community-acquired pneumonia (with airway inflammation/possible small blood) vs severe viral bronchitis**; the right-sided tonsil pain also raises **streptococcal pharyngotonsillitis** as a co-issue.  
Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Suspected community-acquired pneumonia with minor hemoptysis (airway irritation), with possible concomitant streptococcal tonsillitis—await Oxygen_Saturation and Chest_X-Ray to confirm and guide antibiotics.

[DDX]
1. Pneumonia
